description: A subnet the router's DHCP server leases IPv4 or IPv6 addresses of on its interfaces: pools and reservations, the options its clients get, the files PXE clients boot and, for IPv6, the prefixes it delegates to other routers.

bios.description: File of clients with BIOS firmware, of architecture 0 in option 93, loaded over TFTP from server.

ipxe.description: Script or file of clients that run iPXE already, whose user class (option 77) is iPXE; they get it instead of bios and uefi, so that iPXE does not load itself again.

server.description: IPv4 address of the TFTP server the files are on, the DHCP header's next server; needed with bios or uefi, whose firmware loads them over TFTP. null for none, as for an ipxe script of an HTTP URL alone.

uefi.description: File of clients with x86-64 UEFI firmware, of architecture 7 or 9 in option 93, loaded over TFTP from server.

boot.description: Files PXE clients of an IPv4 subnet boot, by firmware; boot files are served elsewhere. null serves none.

x-chalkos-rules.message: boot names no file; give bios, uefi or ipxe, or leave boot out
x-chalkos-rules.rule: self == null || self.bios != null || self.uefi != null || self.ipxe != null

x-chalkos-rules.message: boot's server is no IPv4 address

x-chalkos-rules.description: A boot of BIOS or UEFI files names their server.
x-chalkos-rules.message: boot's bios and uefi files load over TFTP from boot's server; give server

dns.description: DNS servers the clients ask, addresses of the subnet's family.

domain.description: Domain of the clients' names, which they also search; null gives none.

gateway.description: Router the clients route through, inside an IPv4 subnet and neither its network nor its broadcast address; null gives them none. IPv6 clients learn their routers from router advertisements.

interfaces.description: Links the server answers on, each by its full name, without a glob, and once: links of one VRF, each of which a Network document matching it by Name= alone gives a static address in the subnet; one link for an IPv6 subnet. A link takes one subnet of each family.

leaseTime.description: How long a lease lasts, and a delegated prefix: a number and s, m, h or d, 136 years at most. IPv6 clients prefer their addresses for as long.

x-chalkos-rules.description: A lease lasts 4294967295 seconds at most, the longest Kea takes.
x-chalkos-rules.messageExpression: "a lease of " + self + " is longer than 4294967295 seconds, the longest Kea takes"

pools.description: Ranges the server leases addresses from to any client: inside the subnet, apart from each other and from the reservations, and holding none of the subnet's network and broadcast addresses, an IPv6 subnet's first address and the router's, the gateway's and the DNS and boot servers' addresses; empty leases the reservations alone.

last.description: Last address of the pool, no lower than the first.

length.description: Length of each delegated prefix, longer than the range's.

prefix.description: IPv6 range the delegated prefixes are taken from, apart from ::/8, fe80::/10, ff00::/8 and the subnets of the VRF.

prefixDelegation.description: Prefixes the IPv6 server delegates to routers on the link that ask for one, such as a home router's LAN; the router routes each to the link-local address that asked for it, for as long as the lease lasts. null delegates none.

reservations.description: Clients that always get the same address, by their MAC address.

address.description: Address the client always gets, inside the subnet and outside its pools, and none of the subnet's network and broadcast addresses, an IPv6 subnet's first address and the router's, the gateway's and the DNS and boot servers' addresses.

hostname.description: Name the client gets; null gives none.

mac.description: MAC address of the client, in lower case. A DHCPv6 server learns it from the client's DUID or link-local address, which not every client derives from it.
